name: Claim
shortDescription: Request for payment for healthcare services
longDescription: A claim is a request for payment submitted by a patient or healthcare provider for medical services rendered. It includes details about the service, cost, and patient information. Claims are the primary data entity in the lakehouse data processing workflow.

name: Claim Status
longDescription: The status of a claim in the processing workflow. Valid values are: pending (submitted but not yet reviewed), approved (accepted for payment), denied (rejected and will not be paid), in_review (under investigation by claims adjuster). Status transitions follow business rules and require appropriate authorization.

name: Claim Type
longDescription: The type of healthcare service covered by the claim. Valid values are: medical (doctor visits, outpatient procedures, specialists), prescription (medication and pharmaceuticals), hospital (inpatient care, surgery, emergency room). Claim type affects coverage rules and reimbursement rates.

name: Diagnosis Code
longDescription: Standardized ICD-10 (International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision) code representing the medical diagnosis associated with the claim. These codes are used for billing, statistical reporting, and medical record keeping. Format: A00-Z99 with possible subcategories.

name: Provider
longDescription: The healthcare facility, hospital, clinic, or individual physician who provided the medical services for this claim. Provider information includes name, location, and credentials. Providers must be in-network for preferred coverage rates.

name: Claim Amount
longDescription: The total amount in USD requested for reimbursement for the healthcare services provided. Must be a positive decimal value with up to 2 decimal places. Amount is subject to coverage rules, deductibles, copays, and maximum benefit limits.

name: User ID
longDescription: Unique identifier for the user (patient or claims adjuster). Typically an email address format. Used for authentication, authorization, and row-level security to ensure users only see their own claims. This field is critical for data privacy and HIPAA compliance.

name: Patient Name
shortDescription: Name of the patient receiving care
longDescription: Full legal name of the patient who received the healthcare services covered by this claim. Used for identity verification and record keeping. Protected by HIPAA privacy regulations.

name: Claim Date
longDescription: The date on which the healthcare service was provided to the patient. This is distinct from the submission date. Used for determining coverage eligibility and timely filing requirements.

name: Submitted Date
shortDescription: Date claim was submitted for processing
longDescription: Timestamp when the claim was submitted to the insurance company for processing. Used for tracking processing time and ensuring claims are filed within required timelines.

name: Processed Date
longDescription: Timestamp when the claim was fully processed and a determination (approved/denied) was made. Used for performance metrics and compliance reporting.

name: Row-Level Security
shortDescription: Data access control at the row level
longDescription: Security mechanism that restricts which rows of data a user can access based on their identity. Implemented using AWS Lake Formation with session tags. Ensures patients only see their own claims and adjusters only see claims assigned to them. Critical for HIPAA compliance and data privacy.

name: Session Tag
shortDescription: IAM session tag for access control
longDescription: AWS IAM session tag used to pass user identity when assuming an IAM role. The user_id session tag is used by Lake Formation to automatically filter query results to only include rows where user_id matches the session tag value. This provides secure, infrastructure-level row filtering.

name: OAuth Scope
longDescription: OAuth 2.0 scope that defines what operations a user is authorized to perform. Scopes for this system include: claims/query (read claims), claims/submit (create new claims), claims/update (modify claims), claims/approve (approve or deny claims). Scopes are included in JWT tokens and validated by the Gateway interceptor.

name: Bearer Token
longDescription: JSON Web Token (JWT) used for authenticating API requests. Contains user identity, OAuth scopes, and expiration time. Generated by Amazon Cognito and validated by the Gateway interceptor. Tokens expire after 1 hour for security.
